Use one of these quick tools to check how fast your internet is:

- **Speedtest by Ookla** – Available as a free web page and as desktop and mobile apps.  
- **Fast.com (by Netflix)** – A simple, seconds‑long test that shows download speed instantly.  
- **Google’s own speed test** – Grab detailed download, upload, and latency numbers right on the web.  

Pick whichever works best for you, launch it, and you’ll get your current download and upload speeds in a few seconds.

The speed of light in a vacuum is an exact universal constant:

\[
c = 299\,792\,458\ \text{metres per second (m s}^{-1}\text{)}.
\]

It is defined by international agreement (the metre is the distance light travels in vacuum during 1 / 299 792 458 of a second). This speed is the maximum attainable speed for any particle or signal in our universe.

Root Cause
Previously, mathematical calculations were only performed in standard combined search mode if the query matched a strict number and operator regex (which explicitly excluded the = character). Therefore, typing =1+5+3 failed the character validation and was bypassed directly to default web search options.
